symptom: A misspelt statement keyword was not an error. `craete module Foo;` and `dorp entity M.E;` parsed cleanly and did nothing (0 statements, exit 0); `craete persistent entity Shop.Note (Text: string(200));` reported `extraneous input '('` at column 35 instead of at the typo.
cause: `helpStatement: IDENTIFIER (helpTopicWord (DOT? helpTopicWord)*)?` is a utilityStatement alternative, so ANY statement starting with an IDENTIFIER matched it, the rest of the words as the topic; ExitHelpStatement then built nothing for a word other than help/?/exit/quit. The rule is the grammar's catch-all (the #1025 comment already warned it swallows from other statements); a typo is just the case where there is no other statement.
file: `mdl/grammar/MDLParser.g4` (`@parser::members` IsHelpWord), `mdl/grammar/domains/MDLSettings.g4` (semantic predicate on helpStatement), `mdl/visitor/visitor_unknown_statement.go` ("unknown statement 'x' — did you mean 'y'?" when the parser is still in statement/program and ANTLR names the one word), test `mdl/visitor/visitor_session_commands_test.go`
insight: A catch-all alternative that the visitor filters (`switch word { case "help": … }`) is a silent no-op for everything it does not list: move the filter INTO the grammar as a predicate (`{IsHelpWord(p.GetTokenStream().LT(1).GetText())}?`), so the parser, not the visitor, rejects. The words stay IDENTIFIERs — reserving HELP/EXIT/QUIT as tokens would take them away as names everywhere a bare IDENTIFIER is accepted. The generated parser imports no `strings`, so fold case by hand in @members. With the predicate the error lands at the word as `no viable alternative at input 'craete'`, and the listener can rewrite exactly that message when the recognizer's context is StatementContext/ProgramContext. Proof: without the predicate the test reports 3 of 4 inputs parsing to zero statements.
